label: final original token j in long sequences starting with d
explanation: Very sparse feature (52 active steps in 500k dev sequences). It fires almost only on the last original step (to_go==0) when that input is j (86% of mass); the remaining 12% is the <DEL> step of sequences whose first token is d. It is strongly biased toward L=9 (80% of mass at t=8) and toward first token d (75% of mass), with a further boost when s appears early (often at position 2). The top activations (up to 1.54) are d ... j sequences of length 8-9. It never fires in the copy phase or on steps 0-5. Even the most specific conjunction fires on only a small fraction of matching contexts: j-final, L=9, first=d gives precision 0.16 on dev, and adding seen s gives 0.35. So the feature depends on some further combination of the sequence content that I could not capture. Magnitude is higher when first=d and L=9, but I did not pin down what drives it beyond that.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: j, y, t, k, -, p; least: 1, x, z, <DEL>) and the next token to output (most: d, b, s, a, j, u; least: h, 2, m, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=7, L=9 & t=8, t=8.
